skill.description: Deploy Apache Kafka on Kubernetes with the Strimzi operator in KRaft mode. Use it for operator setup, Kafka cluster manifests, topic management, testing, monitoring, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Deploy Kafka on Kubernetes with Strimzi, KRaft mode, topic operations, testing, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are markdown code fences or inline code, not Ruby backtick execution. The guide does use public Strimzi URLs for remote manifests, which is expected but should be version pinned. Additional review found insecure production-style examples for external Kafka TLS and unauthenticated Dapr integration.

remediation.issue: Mutable Strimzi latest manifests are applied from remote URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin Strimzi release URLs or checked-in manifests, and verify checksums before production use.

remediation.issue: The production Kafka example exposes an external NodePort listener with TLS disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Set TLS to true for external listeners and document authentication and network policy requirements.

remediation.issue: The Dapr Kafka component example uses authType none.
remediation.suggestion: Label this as test-only or add authenticated Kafka metadata for production deployments.

remediation.issue: Cleanup instructions delete Kafka PVCs and broker data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear confirmation step, namespace check, and backup warning before PVC deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Production External Kafka Listener
semantic_findings.description: The production cluster example exposes an external NodePort listener with TLS disabled. Applying it as written can expose Kafka traffic without transport encryption.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines are inside the production cluster section and explicitly set type nodeport with tls false. That combination is a clear insecure default for external Kafka access.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Dapr Kafka Component Example
semantic_findings.description: The Dapr integration example sets authType to none without a warning. Users may copy it into environments that require broker authentication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly configures authType none. It may be acceptable in isolated tests, but the guide does not scope it to test-only use.

content.user_title: Deploy Kafka on Kubernetes with Strimzi
content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable path to run Kafka on Kubernetes without missing operator, topic, or test steps. This skill provides Strimzi-based deployment guidance, practical manifests, and validation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Strimzi operator installation in a Kubernetes namespace.
Provides single-node and three-node Kafka cluster configurations.
Shows KafkaTopic CRD creation and topic inspection workflows.
Demonstrates producer and consumer smoke tests with Strimzi images.
Covers service discovery, Prometheus metrics, troubleshooting, and cleanup.
limitations: It does not deploy managed Kafka services such as MSK or Confluent Cloud.
It does not fully configure SASL, ACLs, or certificate management.
It uses public Strimzi latest URLs, so production users should pin versions.
It requires an existing Kubernetes cluster and working kubectl access.

use_cases.title: Create a development Kafka cluster
use_cases.description: Deploy a single-node Strimzi Kafka cluster for service integration testing.

use_cases.title: Plan a Kubernetes Kafka rollout
use_cases.description: Prepare operator installation, broker resources, storage, and readiness checks for a team cluster.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Kafka on Kubernetes
use_cases.description: Check operators, pods, logs, events, topics, and bootstrap services during incidents.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Test Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to deploy a single-node Kafka cluster in the kafka namespace. Include readiness checks and a basic smoke test.

prompt_templates.title: Create Topics and Test Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Kafka topic with three partitions, then outline producer and consumer tests for that topic.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a three-node Strimzi Kafka deployment plan with persistent storage, resource limits, monitoring, and security notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Kafka Kubernetes deployment. Identify risky defaults, missing readiness checks, and safer cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Deploy a development Kafka cluster for integration testing.
output_examples.output: A deployment checklist covering namespace setup, Strimzi installation, single-node Kafka creation, readiness checks, and message testing.

output_examples.input: Prepare Kafka topics for a microservices workflow.
output_examples.output: A topic plan with partitions, replicas, retention settings, bootstrap service names, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a Kafka pod that is not ready.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path covering operator status, pod descriptions, broker logs, Kubernetes events, storage, and memory limits.

best_practices: Pin Strimzi manifests and Kafka image versions before production use.
Enable TLS and authentication for external Kafka listeners.
Test cleanup steps in non-production because PVC deletion removes broker data.
anti_patterns: Do not apply latest remote manifests directly to production clusters.
Do not expose Kafka externally with TLS disabled.
Do not run cleanup commands against shared namespaces without backups.

faq.question: Does this skill support KRaft mode?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide focuses on Strimzi Kafka deployments that use KRaft mode.

faq.question: Can I use it without Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. The workflow assumes a Kubernetes cluster and kubectl access.

faq.question: Does it cover managed Kafka services?
faq.answer: No. It is for self-managed Kafka on Kubernetes, not MSK or Confluent Cloud.

faq.question: Does it create Kafka topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows KafkaTopic CRD usage and topic inspection commands.

faq.question: Is the production example fully secure?
faq.answer: No. Production users should add pinned versions, TLS, authentication, and access controls.

faq.question: Does it include cleanup guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The cleanup section removes Kafka resources, PVCs, the operator, and the namespace.
